decision.summary: The Fed raised its policy rate by 25 basis points, to 1.25%. The vote was 12-0.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 1-1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to keep its target for the federal funds rate at 1 percent.”

changes.quote: The Committee believes that, even after this action, the stance of monetary policy remains accommodative and, coupled with robust underlying growth in productivity, is providing ongoing support to economic activity.

changes.quote: The evidence accumulated over the intermeeting period indicates that output is continuing to expand at a solid pace and labor market conditions have improved.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The evidence accumulated over the intermeeting period indicates that output is continuing to expand at a solid rate and hiring appears to have picked up.”

changes.quote: Although incoming inflation data are somewhat elevated, a portion of the increase in recent months appears to have been due to transitory factors.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Although incoming inflation data have moved somewhat higher, long-term inflation expectations appear to have remained well contained.”

changes.quote: The Committee perceives the upside and downside risks to the attainment of both sustainable growth and price stability for the next few quarters are roughly equal.

tone_quotes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 1-1/4 percent.

The Committee believes that, even after this action, the stance of monetary policy remains accommodative and, coupled with robust underlying growth in productivity, is providing ongoing support to economic activity.
The Committee perceives the upside and downside risks to the attainment of both sustainable growth and price stability for the next few quarters are roughly equal.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 12.67% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.62% and moved -8 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.32% would fall by about $15.63 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 5.6%, and employers added an average of 292k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.9% over the past year (May 2004); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.3% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -13 bp on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates).
